subject: Proposal: temporal evidence & mitigation playbook for p50/p95 hosted API SLOs
messages:
From: Mike O'Neil <mike@helixfinancial.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@helixfinancial.com
Date: Thu, 21 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API SLO: request for temporary relief & evidence submission

Hi Avery / Laura,

Quick context: we have a scheduled card-processing platform migration the week of June 7 that will increase short-lived bursts to Redwood's hosted API. Our ops runbook predicts a concentrated 3–4 hour peak each day for ~3 days. We want to avoid accidental SLO breaches while still keeping production traffic live (can't pause).

Concretely we'd like to request:
- A temporary measurement window carveout or alternate handling for 2026-06-07 → 2026-06-10 covering our account traffic during the migration period,
- If a carveout isn't feasible, a formal patch (temporary p95 threshold relaxation or documented mitigation pathway), and
- Guidance on what telemetry/evidence Redwood needs to consider this request and any credit calculations should an SLO breach occur.

I've attached a short telemetry summary and a CSV of representative traces (helix-telemetry-summary-20260520.csv). We also need to understand how Redwood calculates credits for latency deviation vs. availability credits — Helix procurement will need that for approvals.

Can we get a short run-book for remediation and a proposed terms snippet we can take to procurement? We're hoping to finalize this by EOD Monday (2026-05-24).

Thanks,
Mike
Mike O'Neil
Director, Platform Reliability
Helix Financial
attachments: helix-telemetry-summary-20260520.csv, sample-traces.zip
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
To: Mike O'Neil <mike@helixfinancial.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 21 May 2026 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API SLO: request for temporary relief & evidence submission

Hi Mike — thanks for the note and for sending the sample traces. We've reviewed the CSV at a high level and have a few immediate takeaways + a proposed path forward.

Short answer: we can support a temporary, timeboxed mitigation strategy that avoids an informal "full carveout" (we avoid removing SLOs entirely) but provides:
1) A scoped measurement adjustment for the migration window (2026-06-07 02:00 UTC → 2026-06-10 20:00 UTC) where Helix traffic will be flagged and evaluated with a separate sampling pool for p50/p95 calculation to avoid penalizing unrelated system-wide noise, and
2) A fallback routing policy and burst-mitigation plan (short-term routing to dedicated warm capacity + prefix KV caching configuration) to reduce the expected p95 tail during high burst windows.

What we need from you to finalize an internal proposal and credit model:
- Confirmation of exact migration windows (start/end in UTC) and estimated peak QPS per minute,
- The full telemetry pack you referenced (latency histograms, request ids for sampling), and
- Any procurement constraints (max allowable credit %, preferred credit calculation method: per-hour vs. per-day).

Proposed temporary SLO terms (draft):
- Measurement: Helix traffic will be isolated by customer tag for the listed time window. P50/P95 will be computed on the isolated sample.
- Thresholds: Redwood proposes to keep the p50 commitment unchanged; for p95 we propose a temporary relaxation of +15% on the contractual p95 target during the listed window.
- Evidence & credits: If p95 for the isolated sample exceeds the relaxed threshold, credits will be computed pro-rata on request-count-weighted deviation hours, capped at 10% of monthly invoice for June.
- Canary & rollback: Redwood will run a 2-hour canary on June 6 (pre-migration) using the proposed routing to verify tail latency. If canary fails, automatic rollback to dedicated fallback routing will be activated and we will pause the migration window until a mitigation is confirmed.

I'll pull together a single-page playbook and the credit calc table for your procurement team once you share the telemetry package. Ben / Karthik — flagging this for validation vs standard hosted SLO policy and for any legal/finance constraints around the credit cap above.

Next steps: Mike — please share the full package, and confirm the UTC windows today if possible. We'll aim to have the playbook and proposed DocuSign addendum ready for your review by Monday EOD.

Best,
Avery Johnson
Sr. Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
redwood.ai
From: Mike O'Neil <mike@helixfinancial.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@helixfinancial.com, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API SLO: request for temporary relief & evidence submission

Avery — thanks, that path looks reasonable. Confirming:
- Migration window: 2026-06-07T09:00:00Z → 2026-06-10T17:00:00Z (UTC). Peak expected: ~1.8k QPS sustained for 3-hour segments each day, short spikes up to 3k QPS.
- Procurement note: Helix procurement prefers a deterministic credit formula (per-hour deviation) and a cap they can present to finance. Your 10% cap is in the expected ballpark.

I've uploaded the full telemetry and a short ops runbook to the shared link and attached the summary package (slo-evidence-package-helix-20260521.zip). We'd like the canary on June 6 as you suggested; if you can confirm a two-hour window in UTC we'll schedule our deploys accordingly.

Also: if you can outline the credit example (one page) showing how a single p95 breach over the relaxed threshold translates to a $USD credit, that will speed procurement sign-off.

Thanks —
Mike

Subject: Internal: draft mitigation & evidence playbook for Helix (approve to send)

Team — drafting the final playbook to send to Helix; please review the proposed terms below and reply with corrections by EOD Monday (2026-05-25). If we don't get objections, I'll send this to Mike and include the DocuSign addendum.

Playbook (draft):
1) Scope & Windowing - Helix traffic will be isolated via customer tag for 2026-06-07T09:00:00Z through 2026-06-10T17:00:00Z. Measurement for the purpose of SLO calculation will use an isolated sampling pool (all requests from Helix during that window).

2) Measurement Rules - P50: unchanged (contractual target remains).
  - P95 (temporary): Redwood will apply a relaxed threshold = contractual_p95 * 1.15 for the isolated sample during the window. After the window ends, measurement returns to standard aggregation.
  - Aggregation: p95 will be calculated per 5-minute rolling buckets across Helix-tagged traffic, and then daily-hourly exposure will be summarized for credit calculations.

3) Canary & Fallback - Canary: 2-hour canary on 2026-06-06 (UTC window to be coordinated). Canary will use the proposed routing + caching config. Success criteria: observed p95 <= relaxed threshold on Helix sample for canary period.
  - Fallback: if canary fails, Redwood will automatically route Helix traffic to reserved warm capacity and pause the migration until mitigations are in place.

4) Credits & Calculation (example) - Credit unit: per-hour deviation hours where p95 > relaxed_threshold.
  - Hourly credit = (excess_ms / contractual_p95_ms) * hourly_charge_for_Helix_requests, capped such that total credits for June 2026 <= 10% of the monthly invoice.
  - Example attached (proposed-mitigation-playbook.pdf) shows a worked example converting a 200ms excess at p95 into an hourly credit and a monthly cap.

5) Evidence Required - Full latency histograms (5-minute bins) for Helix-tagged traffic, request-level ids for sampled slow requests, and the canary run logs. Helix has already provided the initial package; we need the complete histograms in CSV form for the exact window.

6) Legal/Finance constraints - Ben / Karthik: confirm whether the 10% cap and per-hour deviation formula is acceptable. Also confirm if we need a different tiered cap for new enterprise customers.

If approved, I'll convert to a 1-page addendum (DocuSign) and include: exact UTC windows, the credit formula, and the canary schedule. Mike has asked for the credit example in USD to speed procurement sign-off.
